title: Fix stale base scene state when repacking a derived scene
body:
## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

- Part of #7984 (open since 2016)

A survey of the open reports in this area found one mechanism behind a group of them. These describe a scene that gains a property override nobody asked for, or that keeps a value the base has moved away from:

> #43032, #93365, #90021, #60846, #41492, #65193, #57089, #7984, #104546

I rebuilt three of these cases in 4.8 and measured them against a stock build. #41492, #43032 and #57089 each fail on stock and pass here. I did not confirm the rest, so the list says where I expect this to help. A second group needs the editor side as well, and the companion PR covers those.

A repack of a derived scene compares the live tree against the snapshot in `base_scene_state`. That snapshot must describe the base version the live tree was really built from. Two things broke that rule.

1. `SceneState` snapshotted a directly inherited base. For a chained base it instead read the state live through `variants[base_scene_idx]->get_state()`. A save replaces the state on the shared `PackedScene`, and the live lookup saw the new state at once.
2. A snapshot alone is not enough. One scene file has one state. Trees built before a save and trees built after a save need different snapshots.

The result: the editor treated inherited values as user edits and wrote spurious property overrides into `.tscn` files. Those overrides stay on disk.

This PR keeps a `Ref` to the base state wherever a state has a `base_scene_idx`, and it copies the state when the base version diverges. PR #107913 works in the same area. Its author describes this state replacement problem correctly and reaches for an uncached `PackedScene` as a workaround. This PR copies the state on divergence instead.

## Additional information

This is the first of two PRs, and it must merge first. The second PR (`fix/editor-reload-base-chain`) reloads editor scenes when a base changes. That PR compares a scene file's modification time against the time recorded in the state derived from it. `get_base_scene_state()` reached through to the live base. The recorded time therefore moved with every save. The comparison could never differ. The second PR is inert without this one.

Both call sites are already editor-only (`p_edit_state != GEN_EDIT_STATE_DISABLED`), so a running game is not affected.

`tests/scene/test_packed_scene.cpp` covers the four nesting shapes, that genuine overrides survive a repack, and that groups and connections still follow the base. It also covers state lifecycle and depth.

**AI use:** I developed this change with AI assistance (Claude) for investigation, implementation and test authoring. I reviewed all of it. I confirmed the behavior by hand in the editor over three rounds of base saves. I also ran the full automated suite (1438 cases, 424492 assertions, passing).
